segment_intel: Fall cleanup and aeration/overseeding are at peak inbound RIGHT NOW (mid-September through October). Multiple shops headline aeration/overseeding as a seasonal exclusive; the booking window is 4-6 weeks, so every missed estimate call is a permanently lost slot.

Snow contract sign-ups run September-November. Shops offering snow removal (common among full-service landscapers) are negotiating winter contracts now; scheduling discipline and fast follow-up win those deals.
Irrigation winterization/blowouts are the other October-November seasonal service; sprinkler-focused shops (sprinkler repair / winterization) see a second inbound bump right after the cleanup wave.

Owner-as-receptionist pattern is heavy in this segment: most independent shops are phone-only or form-only with no email and no booking widget. Estimate requests arrive while crews are on mowers, so missed-call lead capture is the highest-fit angle across nearly every candidate.

Yardbook adoption is real among small lawn shops (Boyd's, Rock N Roots both use it): they get quotes/payments but rent their entire web presence to the platform, which makes the owned-site + direct-capture setup pitch credible.

Directory-only businesses remain a large untapped pool (Fruita/Clifton especially), but per the rules they stay near-misses until an own site or real Facebook Page surfaces; several are phone-only and could convert via FB first-choice channel checks.
